name: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL)
organization: DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL)
description: The DC Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL) is the District’s aging agency and Aging and Disability Resource Center: information and help for residents 60 and older, adults with disabilities and caregivers, including senior centers, meals, transportation, in-home support and legal services.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. TTY users dial 711. Office hours are weekdays 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.
Office: 500 K Street NE, Washington, DC 20002.

name: Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman (Legal Counsel for the Elderly)
organization: Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman (Legal Counsel for the Elderly)
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
Email DCOmbuds@aarp.org. The Attorney General’s 2023 elder justice brochure lists 202-434-2140; the program’s own page gives 202-434-2190.

source_evidence.title: Legal Counsel for the Elderly: The Office of the D.C. Long-Term Care Ombudsman
source_evidence.scope: Phone 202-434-2190 and email; replies within 24 hours or the next business day; serves residents of nursing homes, assisted living and community residence facilities and people on the EPD Medicaid waiver at home; read in full; page updated July 15, 2024. The Attorney General’s elder justice brochure (https://oag.dc.gov/sites/default/files/2024-03/EJS-brochure-updated-08292023-.pdf; updated August 2023; search excerpt) lists 202-434-2140 instead.
